item.text: I’ll make a memory-only pass for omitted passages, then save only new rows to `followup.tsv`. I won’t open or change `list.tsv`.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.28.16	Arabic ء م ن / Hebrew אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary hears a settled refusal to panic inside belief; Isaiah says the one who believes in the tested cornerstone will not hurry in alarm, joining trust to patient footing.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.27.13	Arabic ء م ن / Hebrew אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary grounds waiting in trust that a good outcome is real; the psalmist says he believed he would see the LORD's goodness in the land of the living.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.27.14	wait and take heart	The commentary defines sabır as staying firm until a promised right arrives; the next verse twice calls the hearer to wait for the LORD and tells the heart to be strong.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.33.4	Arabic ء م ن / Hebrew אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary binds a true word to work that fits it; the psalm calls the LORD's word upright and all his work faithful, using אמונה for reliability in action.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.119.86	Arabic ء م ن / Hebrew אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary puts true advice before endurance under attack; the psalmist calls God's commands faithful, אמונה, while pleading for help against false persecutors.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Exod.14.31	Arabic ء م ن / Hebrew אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary connects seeing, confirming, and entering trust; after Israel sees the LORD's great action against Egypt, the people believe in the LORD and Moses.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.33.22	Arabic ح ق ق / Hebrew חקק; table sound correspondence	The commentary joins what is prescribed to refuge from loss; Isaiah names the LORD judge, lawgiver, king, and savior, using מחוקק for the one setting law.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Eccl.4.9	Arabic ع م ل / Hebrew עמל; table sound correspondence	The commentary imagines mutually sustained labor and its due wage; Ecclesiastes says two are better than one because they receive a good return for their toil, עמל.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.4.11	two share warmth	The commentary's harsh winter is endured by people who hold one another; Ecclesiastes asks how one person alone can get warm and says two lying together can.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.17.7	trust as the source of blessing	The commentary calls belief entry into a secure state before the hard road; Jeremiah blesses the person who trusts the LORD and makes him the object of trust.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.17.8	tree survives heat and drought	The commentary's sound vegetation stays green instead of becoming windblown chaff; Jeremiah's trusting person is a tree by water whose leaves stay green and whose fruit does not cease in drought.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.37.3	trust and do good together	The commentary gives separate verbs to belief and good work; the psalm commands trust in the LORD and doing good, then connects these acts with secure dwelling in the land.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezra.7.10	learn, do, then teach	The commentary defines advice as a word passed on for another to perform; Ezra sets his heart to study the LORD's law, do it, and teach its statutes and judgments to Israel.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.30.14	word near mouth and heart to do	The commentary joins a transmitted true word to intentional work; Moses says the command is near in mouth and heart precisely so Israel may do it.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.32.47	word is life, not empty	The commentary insists the inherited instruction is a binding task rather than a disposable suggestion; Moses says the word is no empty thing for the people but their life.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.45.27	sight restores Jacob's trust	The commentary's Yusuf scene turns on whether a report deserves belief; after Jacob initially rejects his sons' news, he sees the wagons Joseph sent and his spirit revives.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.3.28	do not delay a neighbor's due	The commentary makes hak a concrete share owed to another; Proverbs forbids telling a neighbor to return tomorrow when the needed good is already in one's power.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.19.17	giving to poor as loan repaid	The commentary joins debt, benefit to another, and eventual recompense; Proverbs calls kindness to the poor a loan to the LORD that he will repay.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.16.32	rule one's spirit rather than conquer	The commentary's sabır is active self-restraint, and its spear image risks turning truth into force; Proverbs says one slow to anger and ruling his spirit exceeds a mighty city conqueror.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.29.11	wise person holds spirit back	The commentary's vessel rim and stopper picture an inner state kept from spilling out; Proverbs contrasts a fool venting all his spirit with a wise person holding it back.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.141.3	guard at mouth and door of lips	The commentary compares sabır to the stopper that keeps a vessel's contents from escaping; the psalmist asks the LORD to set a guard over his mouth and watch the door of his lips.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.15	patience and soft speech persuade	The commentary turns disputed hak into counsel that does not break the neighbor; Proverbs says patience can persuade a ruler and a soft tongue can break bone.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.50.4	word sustains the weary each morning	The commentary's true advice must hold a companion who weakens and connect one day to the next; the instructed speaker receives a morning-by-morning ear and a word to sustain the weary.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.42.3	fragile reed spared as justice comes	The commentary's rightful load does not crush one too weak to bear it; the servant does not break a bruised reed or extinguish a faint wick while bringing forth justice faithfully.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.42.4	justice established without fainting	The commentary puts endurance after hak because the right must actually arrive; the servant does not grow faint or be crushed until justice is established on earth.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Mal.3.17	those who spoke become treasured on the day	The commentary's mutual truthful speech survives until each person's due day; after the God-fearers speak together, the LORD promises to make them his treasured possession on the appointed day.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Mal.3.18	day distinguishes righteous work	The commentary's final reckoning exposes who actually belongs to the exception; Malachi promises a renewed distinction between righteous and wicked, one serving God and one not.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.9.10	do work before death ends opportunity	The commentary's finite day gives performed work urgency; Ecclesiastes tells the hearer to do with strength what the hand finds because the grave offers no further work.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.11.6	sow morning and evening	The commentary meets day-to-day continuity with patient cultivation; Ecclesiastes says to sow in the morning and not withhold the hand in evening because the grower cannot know which planting will succeed.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.3.17	watchman must pass on warning	The commentary's mutual advice carries a duty to another rather than an optional opinion; Ezekiel is appointed watchman and told to hear God's word and warn Israel on God's behalf.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.3.18	failure to warn leaves bloodguilt	The commentary's hak is a debt one owes the next person; God says the watchman who fails to warn the wicked shares responsibility for the person's death.
strong	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Ezek.18.21	wicked person can turn and live	The commentary says past actions name the rescued group; Ezekiel adds that a formerly wicked person who turns, keeps the statutes, and does justice and righteousness will live, making a changed course decisive.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.58.6	fast releases another's yoke	The commentary calls fasting one form of self-restraint but makes patience an aid to others; Isaiah's chosen fast loosens wicked bonds and lets the oppressed go free.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.3.17	fruit and grain fail	The commentary's patience remains when an expected harvest and wage do not arrive; Habakkuk names fig, vine, olive, field, flock, and herd all failing.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.3.18	joy in God despite failed harvest	The commentary's belief provides refuge when work yields loss; after naming failed crops and herds, Habakkuk says he will still rejoice in the LORD who saves.
strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Makkot 24a	Habakkuk's one principle of faithfulness	The commentary holds belief together with lasting right action; this rabbinic reading says Habakkuk reduced the commandments to the single line that the righteous lives by faithfulness, sharpening the role of אמונה in Habakkuk 2:4.
strong	tevrat	motif	Shabbat 31a	Hillel's reciprocal rule to a convert	The commentary makes advice reciprocal and actionable; Hillel tells the prospective convert not to do to another what is hateful to himself and then sends him to study the rest.
strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Mishnah Avot 5:17	disputes for heaven and disputes for self	The commentary contrasts contending over hak with handing it on; the mishnah distinguishes disputes for Heaven, exemplified by Hillel and Shammai, from Korah's self-seeking dispute, so disagreement itself is not condemned.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 4:28	strive for truth under mortal threat	The commentary couples defending the true word with patience when speaking costs something; Sirach urges fighting for truth even to death and promises God's support.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 6:16	faithful friend as medicine of life	The commentary's bitter remedy and another person's sustaining patience meet in a single image; Sirach calls a faithful friend a medicine of life.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 2:2	steady heart in calamity	The commentary defines sabır as holding oneself in place rather than rushing away; a parent-like instructor tells the learner to set the heart right, remain steadfast, and not become hasty in trouble.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 2:4	patient endurance of humiliation	The commentary puts patience after an acted and spoken right that may bring hardship; Sirach tells the hearer to accept what comes and be patient through humiliating reversals.
strong	tevrat	motif	1 Maccabees 2:50	dying father enjoins children to uphold covenant	The commentary's will joins generations through an actionable word; Mattathias charges his children at death to be zealous for the law and give their lives for the ancestral covenant.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.1.3	work of faith, labor of love, steadfast hope	The commentary orders belief, good work, and patience as defining actions; Paul remembers the community's work of faith, labor of love, and steadfastness of hope together.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.1.3	faith grows and mutual love increases	The commentary moves from individual belief to reciprocal support; Paul thanks God that the congregation's faith grows and the love of every member for one another increases.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.1.4	endurance and faith under persecution	The commentary says the truth people share may have a cost they must help one another bear; Paul boasts of the community's endurance and faith amid persecutions and afflictions.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.5.6	faith active through love	The commentary refuses to leave iman at mere inward assent; Paul says what counts is faith working through love, directly joining belief with outward relation.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.5.22	fruit includes patience and faithfulness	The commentary's joined plants give food through lasting good action; Paul calls love, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, and faithfulness fruit of the Spirit.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.3.18	love in deed and truth	The commentary joins purposeful deeds to a true word passed among people; the letter calls children to love in deed and truth, rather than word or speech alone.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.3.23	believe and love one another	The commentary pairs belief with reciprocal action; this command says to believe in the Son's name and love one another, turning faith into a shared duty.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.3.17	possession withheld from needy sibling	The commentary's hak includes a neighbor's concrete due and its sabır sustains the weak; the letter asks how divine love remains in one who sees a sibling in need yet closes the heart while possessing worldly goods.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2John.1.4	children walking in truth	The commentary's inherited advice should become a walked path; the elder rejoices that some of the addressee's children are walking in truth as commanded by the Father.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2John.1.5	love one another as inherited command	The commentary's will is a binding word passed onward; the elder asks the addressee to love one another, calling it a command held from the beginning.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2John.1.6	love means walking in commands	The commentary says a recommended truth must be worked into conduct; the letter defines love by walking according to the commandments already heard.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.10	service to saints remembered	The commentary's sound work does not disappear when the day's capital runs out; Hebrews says God will not overlook the work and love shown through service to fellow believers.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.12	faith and patience inherit promises	The commentary grounds endurance in a due promise; Hebrews tells the community to imitate those who inherit promises through faith and patience.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.18	flee to refuge and hold hope	The commentary hears both safety and active holding in iman and sabır; Hebrews describes people who have fled for refuge and grasp the hope set before them.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.19	hope as soul's secure anchor	The commentary's vessel stopper and firm rock picture an inner good held against a storm; Hebrews calls hope a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.1	run assigned race with endurance	The commentary's reliable road and intentional work require persistence; Hebrews calls believers to lay aside encumbrance and run their appointed race with endurance.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.2	Jesus endures cross for future joy	The commentary says a trustworthy outcome makes painful patience meaningful; Hebrews presents Jesus enduring the cross for the joy set before him.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.4.2	exhort and correct with patience	The commentary gives true counsel and patience their own places; Paul orders preaching, reproof, rebuke, and exhortation with all patience and teaching.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Tim.6.11	faith, righteousness, love, endurance	The commentary's believer pursues sound conduct and patience together; Paul commands pursuit of righteousness, faith, love, endurance, and gentleness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Titus.2.2	faith, love, and endurance together	The commentary distinguishes believing from holding another through hardship; Titus is to teach older men to be sound in faith, love, and endurance.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.4.19	entrust self while doing good	The commentary binds taking refuge in trust to active good work under suffering; Peter tells those suffering according to God's will to entrust their souls to a faithful creator while doing good.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.2.20	do good and endure unjust suffering	The commentary's patient truth costs its speaker something; Peter says enduring suffering incurred for doing good is pleasing to God.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.3.15	answer with gentleness under pressure	The commentary opposes quarrelling over truth to giving truthful counsel; Peter commands a ready account of hope to questioners, delivered with gentleness and respect.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Col.1.10	walk worthily and bear fruit in good work	The commentary joins road, useful vegetation, and sound action; Paul prays that believers walk worthy of the Lord while bearing fruit in every good work.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Col.1.11	strength for endurance and patience	The commentary says the group must hold its place under pressure; Paul asks that believers receive power for all endurance and patience with joy.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.12.12	hope, endurance in trouble, steady prayer	The commentary's patient waiting is active and grounded in a promised good; Paul calls believers to rejoice in hope, endure affliction, and persevere in prayer.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.6	God repays each by deeds	The commentary's final day gives every person the due of their work; Paul states that God will repay each person according to works.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.5.10	all appear for deeds to be recompensed	The commentary's Hāqqa confronts each worker with what was done; Paul says all must appear before Christ's judgment seat to receive what is due for bodily deeds, good or bad.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.9	God's field and God's building	The commentary specifically meets vegetation with intentional construction; Paul calls the community God's field and God's building in a single verse.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.14	work survives and worker receives wage	The commentary measures the soundness of a worker's deed by whether it lasts through the final day; Paul says the builder whose work survives the fire receives a reward.
strong	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.15	work lost while worker saved	The commentary relates escape from loss to good work that remains; Paul allows a different outcome in which a person's work burns and brings loss while the person is saved through fire.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.25	rock-founded house withstands storm	The commentary's securely fitted work is proved by pressure rather than appearance; Jesus' rock-founded house survives rain, floods, and winds because its foundation holds.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.8.13	rootless believers fall under trial	The commentary's joined green growth needs patient holding after belief; Jesus says the rocky-ground hearers believe for a while but fall away in a time of testing because they lack root.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.3.17	wisdom both peaceable and fruitful	The commentary turns disputed hak into counsel that repairs and yields sound deeds; James calls heavenly wisdom peaceable, gentle, merciful, and full of good fruits.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.3.18	righteous fruit sown in peace	The commentary's linked vegetation and reconciliation are carried by patience; James says a harvest of righteousness is sown in peace by those making peace.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.5.10	prophets speak and endure suffering	The commentary says speaking truth may bring the hardship for which patient support is needed; James offers the prophets who spoke in the Lord's name as examples of suffering and patience.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.5.19	bring wanderer back to truth	The commentary's reciprocal true advice reconnects a person who has broken from the path; James tells the community that someone can bring back a member wandering from the truth.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.5.20	restoration saves from death	The commentary's saving exception is sustained by one person's intervention for another; James says turning a sinner from wandering saves a soul from death and covers sins.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.24.13	endurance to end brings salvation	The commentary's sabır must hold through the whole threatened period; Jesus says the one who endures to the end will be saved.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.14.12	endurance of faithful command-keepers	The commentary orders faith, sound obedience, and patience as traits of those rescued; Revelation calls for the saints' endurance, identifying them as command-keepers who hold faith in Jesus.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.2.10	faithful through death receives life	The commentary's threatened believers ask for patience up to death; the risen speaker tells the persecuted assembly to be faithful unto death and promises the crown of life.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.2.42	teaching and fellowship held together	The commentary makes inherited teaching and communal belonging mutually necessary; the first believers devote themselves to apostolic teaching and fellowship, shared meals, and prayer.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.2.45	goods distributed according to need	The commentary's right includes a share owed to someone lacking support; the believers distribute sale proceeds according to each person's need.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.4.32	one heart and shared possessions	The commentary's individual believers become a connected group in which each can sustain another; Acts describes the multitude of believers as one heart and soul and not claiming possessions as purely private.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.4.34	no needy person among them	The commentary's joined pasture leaves no hungry gap between members; Acts says none of the believers was needy because owners sold property for distribution.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.6.35	do good and lend even to enemies	The commentary's hak includes a debt owed and sabır that can transform an enemy; Jesus commands doing good and lending without expecting return to enemies, and promises a great reward.
strong	incil	motif	Didache 1:3	bless, pray, and fast for persecutors	The commentary's patient answer turns hostility into a healing bond and includes fasting as restraint; the Didache urges blessing cursers, praying for enemies, and fasting for persecutors.
strong	incil	motif	1 Clement 38:2	strong support weak; rich help poor	The commentary's community takes another's weight when that person cannot stand; Clement says the strong should care for the weak and the rich provide for the poor.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.119.90	Arabic ء م ن / Hebrew אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary's advice links generations to something enduring; the psalm joins God's faithfulness, אמונה, through all generations to the firm establishment of the earth.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.119.30	Arabic ء م ن / Hebrew אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary combines trust and a walked right path; the psalmist chooses the way of faithfulness, אמונה, and sets God's judgments before himself.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.112.9	generosity and enduring righteousness	The commentary contrasts capital that shrinks with good action that lasts; the righteous person distributes to the poor and his righteousness endures forever.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.30.15	quiet trust as strength	The commentary defines patience as keeping still without losing confidence; Isaiah says salvation lies in returning and rest, strength in quietness and trust, while the addressees refuse.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.51.7	right instruction in heart without fear	The commentary makes belief a refuge for bearers of true speech; God addresses people with his law in their hearts and tells them not to fear human reproach.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.3.19	warning fulfills duty despite refusal	The commentary makes advice an act owed to another, not control over their response; the watchman who warns the wicked has saved his own life even if the wicked refuses to turn.
medium	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Ezek.18.24	prior righteousness can be abandoned	The commentary says completed actions characterize those excepted from loss; Ezekiel insists that someone once righteous can turn to injustice and die in it, preserving moral reversal beyond a fixed label.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.15.10	give without grudging; work blessed	The commentary connects paying another's due to an unmeasured return; Moses says to give a poor brother generously and without a begrudging heart, promising blessing in the giver's work.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.11.15	surety for stranger brings harm	The commentary's sabır can mean standing guarantor for another's debt; Proverbs warns that pledging oneself for a stranger brings suffering, providing a limit to that secondary image.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.2.10	receive adversity without sinful speech	The commentary defines patience as restraining the inner cry under an inescapable blow; Job rebukes his wife for accepting good but rejecting adversity from God and does not sin with his lips.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.3.16	wait quietly for the day of trouble	The commentary's patience remains still before a promised day even with bodily alarm; Habakkuk trembles at the vision yet resolves to wait quietly for the day of distress.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.3.19	secure footing on dangerous heights	The commentary's dependable load animal and mountain stand for not stumbling under pressure; Habakkuk calls God his strength and says he makes his feet like a deer's on the heights.
medium	tevrat	motif	Sirach 2:6	trust followed by straight course	The commentary joins iman to a road that can be walked patiently; Sirach directs the son to trust God for help and make his ways straight.
medium	tevrat	motif	Sirach 29:15	guarantor gives his life for another	The commentary develops sabır as a friend who underwrites someone else's debt; Sirach tells the debtor not to forget the guarantor's kindness because that person has put life at risk for him.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 1:14	selfhood requires more than oneself	The commentary says belief and work can be individual but saving advice must pass between people; Hillel asks what a person is if only for himself.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 1:2	world stands on teaching and kindness	The commentary's sound community combines a true word with useful action; the mishnah names Torah, worship, and acts of lovingkindness as supports on which the world stands.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Bava Metzia 30b	legal right alone does not repair society	The commentary moves hak from winning a dispute toward mutually owed care; the Talmud says Jerusalem's downfall was connected to judging by strict law without going beyond its letter.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 2:19	test the righteous person's forbearance	The commentary says speaking right may bring hostile blows and demand patience; the opponents in Wisdom propose insult and torture to test the righteous person's gentleness and endurance.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 3:5	testing followed by great reward	The commentary's bitter medicine and earned due meet in suffering that proves worth; Wisdom says the righteous, disciplined for a little while, receive great good after God tests them.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.5	add virtue to faith	The commentary moves from believing to work of a specified quality; Peter asks believers to supplement faith with virtue rather than leave faith unworked.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.6	self-control and endurance	The commentary defines sabır as first holding oneself, then remaining in place; Peter's sequence moves from knowledge to self-control and from self-control to endurance.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.7	endurance grows into mutual affection	The commentary's self-restraint becomes a bond with the next person; Peter's sequence leads from endurance to godliness, sibling affection, and love.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.4.9	struck down but not destroyed	The commentary's patient person remains held under a blow; Paul describes believers as persecuted yet not abandoned and struck down yet not destroyed.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.4.16	inward renewal each day	The commentary joins the passing day with an inner good kept from loss; Paul says that even as the outer person wastes away the inner person is renewed day by day.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.4.17	brief suffering and weight of glory	The commentary's right load, labor, and reward meet in a paradox; Paul says momentary affliction prepares an eternal weight of glory beyond comparison.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.4.18	unseen enduring reality	The commentary contrasts passing worldly capital with something that remains; Paul directs attention from seen temporary things to unseen eternal ones.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.11	diligence until hope's fulfillment	The commentary says patient action must hold to the end of the day; Hebrews asks each hearer to show the same diligence for full assurance of hope until the end.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.1	faith as assurance of hoped reality	The commentary hears trust in the truth of a promise before it arrives; Hebrews defines faith by confidence concerning what is hoped for and conviction about what is not seen.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.3.10	teaching, conduct, faith, patience together	The commentary binds an advised truth to practiced action and endurance; Paul reminds Timothy that he observed Paul's teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, and steadfastness.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.4.7	race finished and faith kept	The commentary makes repeated work over time a defining completed act; Paul says he fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.4.8	righteous crown due on the day	The commentary's finished work and patient wait meet a day of due recompense; Paul says the righteous judge will award him the crown on that day.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.12.11	testimony held despite death	The commentary's true word can become a defended standard under mortal threat; the faithful conquer by their testimony and do not cling to life even when facing death.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.24.12	lawlessness cools mutual love	The commentary's patience keeps connected people from splitting apart; Jesus says increasing lawlessness makes the love of many grow cold before his call to endure.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.25.35	feed hungry and welcome stranger	The commentary tests whether a sound deed nourishes the next person; the king names feeding, giving drink, and welcoming as acts that mark those accepted at judgment.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.25.40	care for least counted as service	The commentary's mutual support gives a needy neighbor a concrete claim; the king identifies deeds done for the least of his brothers with deeds done for him.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.2.44	believers gather with things in common	The commentary's scattered patches become a joined group; Acts says believers stay together and hold their possessions in common before describing need-based distribution.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.4.35	proceeds placed for need-based distribution	The commentary's shared hak is an actual material due; believers lay sale proceeds at the apostles' feet and distribution is made according to need.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Mark.8.35	life lost for true message is saved	The commentary's rescue from loss can require holding fast under threat; Jesus says one who loses life for him and the gospel will save it.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.8	contentious people reject truth	The commentary contrasts handing on hak with pulling it into a dispute; Paul describes the self-seeking as disobedient to truth and obedient to injustice.

medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.1	faith as assurance of hoped reality	The commentary hears trust in the truth of a promise before it arrives; Hebrews defines faith by confidence concerning what is hoped for and conviction about what is not seen.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.3.10	teaching, conduct, faith, patience together	The commentary binds an advised truth to practiced action and endurance; Paul reminds Timothy that he observed Paul's teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, and steadfastness.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.4.7	race finished and faith kept	The commentary makes repeated work over time a defining completed act; Paul says he fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.4.8	righteous crown due on the day	The commentary's finished work and patient wait meet a day of due recompense; Paul says the righteous judge will award him the crown on that day.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.12.11	testimony held despite death	The commentary's true word can become a defended standard under mortal threat; the faithful conquer by their testimony and do not cling to life even when facing death.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.24.12	lawlessness cools mutual love	The commentary's patience keeps connected people from splitting apart; Jesus says increasing lawlessness makes the love of many grow cold before his call to endure.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.25.35	feed hungry and welcome stranger	The commentary tests whether a sound deed nourishes the next person; the king names feeding, giving drink, and welcoming as acts that mark those accepted at judgment.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.25.40	care for least counted as service	The commentary's mutual support gives a needy neighbor a concrete claim; the king identifies deeds done for the least of his brothers with deeds done for him.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.2.44	believers gather with things in common	The commentary's scattered patches become a joined group; Acts says believers stay together and hold their possessions in common before describing need-based distribution.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.4.35	proceeds placed for need-based distribution	The commentary's shared hak is an actual material due; believers lay sale proceeds at the apostles' feet and distribution is made according to need.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Mark.8.35	life lost for true message is saved	The commentary's rescue from loss can require holding fast under threat; Jesus says one who loses life for him and the gospel will save it.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.8	contentious people reject truth	The commentary contrasts handing on hak with pulling it into a dispute; Paul describes the self-seeking as disobedient to truth and obedient to injustice.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.8.14	wealth chokes plant before fruit	The commentary contrasts capital that distracts with useful fruit that lasts; Jesus says life's cares, riches, and pleasures choke the heard word so its hearers fail to mature fruit.
medium	incil	motif	Ignatius, Letter to Polycarp 1:2	athlete bears infirmities of all	The commentary's guarantor carries another's weakness and its worker anticipates gain; Ignatius urges Polycarp to bear everyone's infirmities like a trained athlete and links harder labor to greater gain.
medium	incil	motif	Ignatius, Letter to Polycarp 3:1	anvil holds through repeated blows	The commentary's hard stone and straight blow make patience a strength under impact; Ignatius compares the addressed leader to an anvil that receives strikes and stays firm.
medium	incil	motif	1 Clement 34:2	worker receives bread for labor	The commentary's day of work comes to its wage; Clement contrasts the diligent worker who can receive bread from the employer with the idle one who cannot face him.
medium	incil	motif	Justin Martyr, First Apology 67	shared funds sustain people in need	The commentary's reciprocal counsel must become practical provision; Justin describes a gathered Christian community collecting voluntary gifts for orphans, widows, the sick, strangers, and prisoners.
medium	incil	motif	Tertullian, Apology 39	common fund cares for vulnerable	The commentary's linked pasture feeds people unable to sustain themselves; Tertullian describes voluntary community contributions used for the poor, bereaved, aged, shipwrecked, and imprisoned.
weak	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 4:16	world as antechamber for coming world	The commentary's brief working day prepares an enduring recompense; this saying makes the present world a vestibule in which a person prepares for the next, though its architectural image only indirectly meets the commentary's work-and-wage scene.
weak	incil	motif	Shepherd of Hermas, Mandate 5.1	patience rules anger and supports right acts	The commentary's sabır restrains the inner eruption before it harms others; Hermas contrasts patience with anger and connects patience with righteous conduct, though subsection numbering varies among editions.
